name: cinematic-scroll
description: Web Design Studio is an Agent Skill for distinctive websites, interactive 3D and motion. It builds standalone HTML or Next.js experiences with deliberate art direction, scroll choreography, parallax, WebGL/WebXR scenes, responsive fallbacks, design tokens, verification tools and an optional five-phase production workflow. The established cinematic-scroll identifier remains the install and compatibility key.
maintenanceNote: Open-source, actively developed. Community contributions and feedback welcome.

invokeWhen: User asks to BUILD a cinematic/scroll-driven/parallax/3D-tilt/environment-morphing website, launch or release page, product story, or editorial microsite
User asks to AUDIT, review, or score the scroll experience of a specific URL or local build they own or are authorized to test
User asks to plan a cinematic motion storyboard, integrate scroll motion into an existing app, or improve a cinematic build
User references the flagship/WebXR/3D scroll experience or asks to generate 3D chapter assets in the Next.js template
doNotInvokeFor: Generic landing pages, CRUD apps, forms/wizards, CMS integrations, dashboards, or admin panels
Any request without explicit scroll-driven motion or cinematic web-design intent
Auditing arbitrary third-party URLs the user does not own or have authorization to test
exampleTriggers: Build a cinematic scroll release page for <product> in a <style> aesthetic
Audit the scroll experience of <a URL I own> and score pacing/perf/a11y/arc

security.note: All sensitive capabilities are optional and user-initiated. FAL_KEY is a billable secret — store it in a gitignored .env.local or a secret manager, never in source or version control. Audit mode uses the agent's own browser/fetch access to analyze a user-supplied URL (not a local headless binary); the request may trigger analytics or side effects on the target — only audit sites you own or are authorized to test. Mode A output pages load GSAP + ScrollTrigger and three.js from cdn.jsdelivr.net, the three.js Draco decoder and @google/model-viewer from unpkg.com, and Google Fonts from fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com (SRI-pinned where the format allows — ES-module import maps cannot carry SRI) — self-host these if your deployment policy requires it. See manifest.md → Security & Privacy and audit-mode.md.

thirdPartyNetworkCalls.when: Optional TasteHQ brand analysis and verification
thirdPartyNetworkCalls.destination: www.tastehq.w230.net/api/query and /api/score (or explicitly configured compatible service)
thirdPartyNetworkCalls.trigger: in-scope brand matching or a required project taste contract; sends supplied brief/URLs/grammar; no key required by the adapter, no background memory
user-initiated, explicit confirmation required. Learn mode uses this same browser/fetch access to observe user-authorized URLs; no additional network exception is introduced.

thirdPartyNetworkCalls.destination: cdn.jsdelivr.net (GSAP + ScrollTrigger, three.js), unpkg.com (three.js Draco decoder, @google/model-viewer), fonts.googleapis.com + fonts.gstatic.com (Google Fonts)
thirdPartyNetworkCalls.trigger: loaded by the generated HTML when opened in a browser — self-host to avoid

modes.name: Scroll artifact
modes.description: Single self-contained HTML or .tsx scroll section / page. No build step, no AI keys. Generated pages load GSAP and Google Fonts from third-party CDNs (SRI-pinned). Fast preview.

modes.name: Full release site
modes.description: Next.js App Router templates work with static or demo assets without keys. Optional fal.ai generation requires your own fal.ai account and FAL_KEY and makes outbound calls to fal.ai.

modes.name: Cinematic audit
modes.description: Agent-driven analysis of an existing URL's scroll experience using the agent's browser/fetch access. Scores pacing, performance, accessibility, and emotional arc. Outputs remediation-plan.md with prioritized fixes. This is not a standalone CLI tool.

pipeline.gatedNote: Review checkpoints apply when requested. Otherwise complete the result autonomously; resolve material ambiguity from project context or ask a focused question. A small section needs decisions and evidence, not mandatory phase documents. Full stories can use one project note; separate artifacts below are for staged or complex work. Optional Phase 0 resolves the TasteHQ brand contract.
